subject: [Bugfix]  Fix precision corruption when shared_experts_stream=None (#28942)
pr_body:
# Fix Precision issues When shared_experts_stream=None

## Purpose

Fix precision issues when `shared_experts_stream=None` by executing shared experts before routed experts kernel, preventing hidden_states from being mutated in-place.

## Test Plan

Tested on ROCm (gfx942) with DeepSeek-R1 model using TP=8.

### Start vLLM Server

```bash
export GPU_ARCHS=gfx942
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0
MODEL=path/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1

AITER_ENABLE_VSKIP=0 \
VLLM_USE_V1=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve $MODEL \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --disable-log-requests \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --block-size 1 \
  --enforce-eager \
  2>&1 | tee vllm_serve.log
```

### Send Test Request

```bash
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/v1/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "The capital of China",
    "temperature": 0,
    "top_p": 1,
    "top_k": 0,
    "repetition_penalty": 1.0,
    "presence_penalty": 0,
    "frequency_penalty": 0,
    "stream": false,
    "ignore_eos": false,
    "n": 1,
    "seed": 123
  }'
```

subject: [Bugfix][Model] Restore causal image SWA for DeepSeek V4.1 (#57152)
pr_body:
## Summary

Restore causal sliding-window attention for image tokens in DeepSeek V4.1 VL.

V4.1 inherited the image visibility rules used by DeepSeek V4 Vision-Exp: tokens inside an image could attend to earlier image tokens outside the sliding window and to future image tokens. This differs from the [official V4.1 reference implementation](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277/inference/model.py#L410), where `_window_kv` uses `get_window_topk_idxs` and both image and text tokens attend to the same causal window. With a window of 128, query position `p` should see only `[max(0, p - 127), p]` through SWA.

The incorrect widening affects full-image prefill as well as continuation chunks. For example, at the beginning of image span `[1900, 3948)`, the inherited rule exposes future image tokens through position 3947; the V4.1 reference permits only positions 1773 through 1900.

The key line in the [official `get_window_topk_idxs`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277/inference/model.py#L421) is:

```python
idxs = torch.where(idxs > end, -1, idxs)
```

The reference masks every index greater than the query position with `-1`; this is a causal 128-token window, including the current token. Executing the published `get_window_topk_idxs` at query position 1900 produces exactly 128 indices, from 1773 through 1900, with no future positions.

## Changes

- Disable multimodal prefix-LM/bidirectional-range configuration for V4.1.
- Make the shared SWA metadata builder respect an explicit `is_mm_prefix_lm=False`, keeping V4.1 metadata and paged indices causal.
- Set the V4.1 attention-side image window extension to zero. Image preprocessing, the vision encoder, and `vision_max_n_token` remain unchanged.
- Keep the existing causal gather lengths and workspace sizes. The final diff does not change NVIDIA or AMD workspace allocation.
- Add six regression cases: full prefill and continuation prefill, each with compression ratios `0/1/2`. Verify causal key positions in both gathered and paged indices, gather/CPU-plan consistency, and absence of image visib …[truncated]

subject: [Misc] Fixes and Optimizations for DeepEP + DeepGEMM combination. (#19298)
pr_body:
## Purpose
### Issue1:
  The engine fails to initialize with DeepseekR1 + data-parallel-size 32 + expert-parallel + VLLM_ALL2ALL_BACKEND="deepep_high_throughput" + VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1

#### Cause:
  During profile runs we execute model forward pass on all GPUs with maximum batch size. We do this with dummy input_ids all set to zeros. This has an effect of routing all tokens from all GPUs to a specific set of experts / GPU Ranks in the All2All dispatch call. The GPU receiving all the tokens has an enormous batch-size to process. The GPUs OOM as a result.

### Issue2:
   The engine fails to initialize with DeepseekR1 + data-parallel-size 128 + expert-parallel + VLLM_ALL2ALL_BACKEND="deepep_low_latency" + VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1

### Issue 3:
  CUDA illegal memory access in FP8 block-quant triton kernel

#### Cause:
   Integer overflow issues in the block-quant triton kernel.

### Changes / Fixes:
  - [issue1 - fix] Randomize _dummy_run input_ids() 
     - Randomize dummy run input IDs. This is so all experts of the model and consequently the GPU ranks, receive a balanced number of tokens.

    - DeepEP High Throughput Prepare/Finalize : Remove expensive torch ops in finalize function
  - [issue2 - fix] Ask DeepEP for `num_rdma_bytes` hint
     - DeepEP should give us the right requirements. 
  - [issue3 - fix] Use int64 in offset calculations (stride multiplication) in the fp8 block-quant kernels.

subject: [Bugfix][cache_kernels]: Fix OOB in cache_kernels.cu (#28760)
pr_body: ## Purpose This PR fixes a potential out-of-bounds (OOB) memory access in the gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache CUDA kernel, as originally reported in Issue #27909. The bug was identified by static analysis. The root cause was that the offset (calculated from seq_starts[bid] / block_size) was not validated against the block_table_stride (the bound of the block table) before being used to access the batch_block_table pointer. 1. this fix calculates a safe upper bound (loop_end) before the loop starts, using std::min((int64_t)full_blocks_end, block_table_stride - offset). This ensures the loop never iterates past the safe boundary. 2. For the partial block: A standard bounds check (if (offset + full_blocks_end < block_table_stride)) is added to secure the final OOB access after the loop. ## Test Plan 1. Unit Test Verification: A new unit test (tests/kernels/test_cache_kernels.py::test_gather_cache_oob) was added to specifically reproduce the exact boundary condition described in the issue (where seq_starts causes the offset to point near the end of the table). 2. Benchmark & Accuracy Verification Device: NVIDIA A100 PCIe Models: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (To verify no regression on Dense models). Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat (To verify fix impact on MoE architectures). Metrics: lm_eval (GSM8K) for accuracy and vllm bench serve for throughput/latency. ## Test Result 1. Sanitizer Verification The fix was verified by running the new unit test under compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck. After fix: The test passes, and compute_sanitizer reports no errors, confirming the OOB access is resolved. `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_cache_kernels.py` 2. Benchmark & Accuracy Report I performed a comprehensive benchmark on NVIDIA A100 PCIe. Llama-3.1-8B (Dense): Shows no regression. Accuracy and performance remain stable, confirming the fix is safe for general use. Qwen1.5-MoE (MoE): Shows improved accuracy (+4% strict match) and higher throughput (~10%). subject: fix: reorder DSA indexer dual-stream ops to avoid CUDA graph stream explosion (#30025)
pr_body:
## Motivation

On GLM-5.2 (DSA) with EAGLE speculative decoding, the profiler shows ~22 CUDA
streams during target verify instead of the expected 2. This appeared after the
DSA indexer Q/K fusion landed.

The root cause is the issue order of the dual-stream section in the fused
indexer path `Indexer._fused_q_prepare_and_store`. The second overlap stage
enqueued the alt-stream fused-K + KV-cache store **before** the main-stream
fused-Q kernel. During CUDA-graph capture, that ordering makes
`cudaGraphInstantiate` reserve a fresh side stream for each layer's fork
(~22 total) instead of reusing a single one.

## Modification

Reorder the second overlap stage in `_fused_q_prepare_and_store` so the
main-stream fused-Q kernel is enqueued **before** the alt-stream fused-K +
KV-cache store. This is a pure scheduling reorder — no numerics change — and it
lets graph capture reuse one alt stream, collapsing the captured graph from
~22 streams back to 2 while preserving the Q‖K dual-stream overlap
(max concurrent worker = 2).

## Benchmark

GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, EAGLE (steps 5 / topk 1 / draft 6), `generated-shared-prefix`
(sys 73360 / q 6640), output-len 220, `--max-concurrency 1`. Each config was
launched once and benchmarked **N=10** times; Welch's t-test vs HEAD.

Note: `TPOT = per_step_cost / accept_len`, and `accept_len` has a genuine
run-to-run noise floor (~±3%) from non-deterministic GPU reductions in spec
decoding, so the confound-free comparison is per-step verify cost
(`TPOT x accept_len`).

**Accept length** (N=10)

| config | mean | std | vs HEAD | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HEAD (fused, 22 streams) | 2.810 | 0.079 | — | — |
| fusion-off (`SGLANG_DISABLE_DSA_INDEXER_FUSION=1`) | 2.803 | 0.094 | -0.26% (t=+0.19) | noise |
| **fix (reorder, 2 streams)** | 2.865 | 0.087 | +1.96% (t=-1.48) | noise |

**Mean TPOT (ms)** (N=10)

| config | mean | std | vs HEAD | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HEAD | 4.208 | 0.127 | — | — |
| fusion-off | 4.345 | 0.154 | +3.26% (t=-2.17) | slower |
| **fix** | 4.133 | 0.115 | -1.78% (t=+1.39) | noise |

**Per-step verify cost = TPOT x accept_len (ms)** — confound-free, high powe …[truncated]

subject: Fix KV-canary workspace accounting after graph capture (#38596)
pr_body:
## Motivation

Eager KV-canary forwards allocate plans after post-capture KV sizing has assigned the available memory to the KV pool. On large pools, this unaccounted workspace can approach a gigabyte and cause an otherwise memory-tight configuration to OOM.

## Modifications

Compute the workspace from the installed `VerifyPlan`, `WritePlan`, `ExpectedInputs`, and `PlanInput` capacities, and subtract it in addition to the existing headroom. Target and draft forwards execute sequentially, so reserve their largest workspace. Canary-disabled configurations retain exactly the same byte budget.

Canary capacities remain fixed across post-capture resizing. The reserve uses those actual capacities, including the three verify entries per pool slot.

Add regression coverage for allocation byte counts, pool-slot scaling, additive headroom, canary-disabled budgets, and draft-runner forwarding.

## Accuracy Tests

- Sizing, headroom, startup, and capacity tests: **82 passed, 50 subtests passed**.
- Canary unit and kernel tests on GB300: **390 passed, 23 subtests passed**.
- Canary mock tests: **9 passed**; E2E helper tests: **2 passed**.
- Final startup-forwarding test rerun: **22 passed, 18 subtests passed**.
- `python -m pytest -q test/registered/mem_cache/test_post_capture_kv_sizing.py`: **3 passed** in 178.97 s, including the GSM8K accuracy check. Post-capture sizing backed a 230.25 GiB KV pool.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING=1 python -m pytest -q test/registered/kv_canary/test_self_e2e_baseline.py::TestBaselineMha`: **1 passed** in 193.80 s.
- `pre-commit run`: passed.

Server tests used a separate environment with the upstream PyTorch 2.13 and kernel dependencies. No multi-GPU, SWA, speculative, or disaggregated serving validation was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark or profiling run.

subject: [NPU] Fix DSA top-k seed buffer shape for MTP IndexShare (#31005)
pr_body:
## Motivation
PR #29787 introduced DSA top-k seed reuse from draft-extend to avoid recomputing the DSA indexer top-k in the draft-decode loop.

The seed buffers were allocated using the CUDA-style 2D layout:

```text
[num_tokens, index_topk]
```
However, the Ascend lightning indexer and sparse attention use a 3D TND sparse-index layout:
```text
[num_tokens, index_kv_heads, index_topk]
```
For the current NPU DSA implementation, the Index KV cache uses one MQA head, so the expected NPU seed shape is:
```text
[num_tokens, 1, index_topk]
```
The incorrect buffer shape caused two startup failures during graph capture:
With speculative_num_steps=1, copying the draft-extend indexer output into the 2D seed buffer failed with a broadcast shape error.
With speculative_num_steps>1, draft-decode graph capture passed a 2D sparse_indices tensor to npu_sparse_flash_attention, which requires a 3D tensor.
This PR enables NPU to use the draft-extend DSA seed reuse feature without disabling the optimization.

## Modifications

Updated the draft-extend graph capture buffer to use the platform-native seed shape.
Updated the draft-decode graph seed buffer to use the same platform-native shape.
Updated the eager draft-extend seed buffer allocation and reallocation logic to preserve all trailing dimensions.
Added validation for missing index_topk configuration.
Kept the existing NPU Draft Extend → Draft Decode DSA top-k reuse path enabled.
The NPU middle dimension is derived from the Index KV cache contract rather than index_n_heads. index_n_heads describes the lightning indexer's query heads, while sparse attention expects the sparse-index N dimension to match the single-head MQA Index KV cache.

subject: fix(fa3): no NaN embeddings with fa_skip_kv_cache under piecewise CUDA graph (#27343)
pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes NaN embeddings emitted by the `fa_skip_kv_cache` embedding fast path (added in #21971) when **piecewise CUDA graph** is enabled. ~40% of **short** embedding inputs came back as fully-NaN vectors; long inputs were unaffected.

## Root cause

`fa_skip_kv_cache` serves attention with `flash_attn_varlen_func` on raw K/V. Under a piecewise CUDA graph the model forward runs at a **padded token-bucket size**, so the query tensor `q` has more rows (`B`) than `cu_seqlens_q` covers (`N`, the real token count).

`flash_attn_varlen_func` requires `q.shape[0] == cu_seqlens_q[-1]`. With `N < B` that contract is violated, and the boundary query block corrupts the **last real token's** output. Embedding models use LAST-token pooling, so that corrupted row *is* the returned embedding → NaN.

Only short inputs are affected: long inputs fill the top bucket (no padding / the boundary lands harmlessly), while short inputs get padded into a small bucket, placing the last real token right at the corrupting boundary. It reproduces only with the FA3 backend (the flashinfer backend is already piecewise-padding-aware), and is independent of `--prefill-only-disable-kv-cache` (it is gated on the embedding config, not that flag).

## Fix

Append the padded tail `[N, B)` as a **dummy, self-attending segment** so `cu_seqlens = [0, …, N, B]` and `q.shape[0] == cu_seqlens_q[-1]` holds again. The real-token segments are untouched (their attention is unchanged), and the padding rows get valid, isolated self-attention instead of reading uninitialized memory. This mirrors how the flashinfer backend reserves a dummy request for piecewise padding.

## Validation

H100, Qwen3-0.6B embedding model (fp16), fa3 + piecewise:

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| previously-NaN short inputs | 81/81 NaN | **0** |
| overall NaN | ~40% of short | **0/1000** |
| cosine vs non-piecewise (correct) path | — | **mean 0.9999987, min 0.9999946** (all 1000 ≥ 0.99999) |

So the fix removes the NaN *and* leaves correct embeddings bit-for-bit equivalent.

## Test

Adds `test/registered/prefill_only/test_fa_skip_kv_cache_piecewise_nan.py`:
- `test_no_nan_with_piecewise` — short inputs (~1–150 toke …[truncated]

subject: [ROCm] fix sleep mode not releasing GPU memory problem on ROCm  (#37533)
pr_body: ## Purpose On ROCm, `hipMemRelease` does not return physical VRAM to the free pool while the virtual-address reservation (from `hipMemAddressReserve`) is still held. This causes sleep mode to report memory as freed at the HIP runtime level, but the GPU VRAM remains occupied at the hardware level (confirmed via `rocm-smi`), preventing other applications (e.g. RL training frameworks) from using the freed memory. Cycle `cuMemAddressFree` → `cuMemAddressReserve` (requesting the same address) at the end of `unmap_and_release` on the ROCm path. This forces the driver to actually release the physical pages while immediately re-reserving the same virtual address so that a subsequent `create_and_map` (wake_up) works without changing any tensor pointers. Only the `#else` (USE_ROCM) branch of `unmap_and_release` is modified — no impact on the NVIDIA CUDA path. ## Test Plan Use the following script can reproduce the problem. Below is the script: ``` import torch from vllm import LLM if __name__ == '__main__': llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", enable_sleep_mode=True) def run_inference(prompt): outputs = llm.generate(prompt) for output in outputs: prompt = output.prompt generated_text = output.outputs[0].text print(f"Prompt: {prompt!r}, Generated text: {generated_text!r}") torch.cuda.empty_cache() run_inference("San Francisco is") llm.sleep() torch.cuda.empty_cache() llm.wake_up() torch.cuda.empty_cache() run_inference("Paris is") ``` Tested on MI300X (8 GPUs) with ROCm 7.2, PyTorch 2.10, vLLM v0.17.1.dev0 - `rocm-smi` confirms VRAM% drops from 90% → 0% after sleep (previously stayed at 89%) - `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` reports 172 GiB freed immediately - wake_up + inference works correctly after sleep - Both level-1 and level-2 sleep verified - Tested with `VLLM_ROCM_SLEEP_MEM_CHUNK_SIZE=256` ## Test Result before using our patch, gpu_workers.py will show by torch.cuda.mem_get_info() the physical memory will not release after sleeping: An …[truncated]

subject: [AMD][Kernel][Bugfix] Cast offsets tensor bn to tl.int64 to avoid GPU segfault (#23692)
pr_body: The tensor loaded into `bn ` is multiplied by `stride_k_cache_bs `in the `_fwd_kernel `in `prefix_prefill.py` and produces an integer overflow resulting in negative offsets which result in a GPU segfault.  Changing `stride_k_cache_bs  `to be `tl.int64` in the function signature did **not** work.  Casting the `bn` tensor to `tl.int64` fixes the problem.  I added some additional casts into `_fwd_kernel_flash_attn_v2 `and `_fwd_kernel_alibi` as well.

subject: Fix: Safe RoPE Cache Expansion to Prevent Position-ID Out-of-Bounds in EAGLE + Long-Sequence Workloads (#11871)
pr_body:
## Motivation



## Modifications

This PR fixes an issue introduced in [#10788](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/10788).

In [#10788](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/10788) RoPE pre-expansion length was calculated using
`req_to_token_pool.max_context_len` at first place, which turned out to be unstable and sometimes larger than the model’s true context window (base_ctx).

Because max_context_len is runtime-dependent, the runners could read different values which cause their RoPE caches to have different sizes before CUDA-graph capture.

That mismatch broke EAGLE’s verification path and led to repeated invalid eagle tree warnings and a failing test_gsm8k.

Use the model’s static limit `base_ctx` when computing the RoPE reserve length:

```
reserve = base_ctx + steps * draft * SAFETY_FACTOR + MARGIN
```

subject: [Bugfix] Allocate packed outputs in fused_q_kv_rmsnorm so q_b_proj keeps its low-latency GEMM path at decode (#53109)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a silent performance bug: `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` allocates its outputs with `torch.empty_like(qr)`, but `qr`/`kv` are column slices of the fused `qkv_a` projection output. PyTorch preserves the strides of size-1 dims, so at `num_tokens == 1` (single-sequence decode) `empty_like` returns a tensor carrying the **parent buffer's row stride** — e.g. `(2112, 1)` for a `[1, 1536]` `q_c` slice:

```python
>>> qkv = torch.empty(1, 2112)
>>> q = qkv[:, :1536]
>>> torch.empty_like(q).stride()
(2112, 1)   # is_contiguous() is True, but not packed row-major
```

The Kimi-K3 low-latency GEMM dispatch (`low_latency_gemm._is_packed_row_major`, which requires `stride == (shape[1], 1)`) then rejects `q_c`, and `q_b_proj` silently falls back to `F.linear` → cuBLAS on **every decode step**, even though `(2304, 1536)` is listed in `KIMI_K3_PROJECTIONS`. `num_tokens >= 2` happens to produce packed strides, so only decode is affected — which is why this never showed up in prefill or batched benchmarks.

The fallback is not just a missed fusion. On one SM103 machine (148 SMs) the cuBLAS heuristic picks `nvjet_sm103_tst_16x64_64x16_2x1_v_bz_TNN` at ~10.9 µs/call for this `[1,1536]×[1536,2304]` GEMM, vs 4.5 µs (in-graph) for the intended `dsv3_fused_a` kernel — ~150 µs per decode step across Kimi-K3's 24 MLA layers at TP8. On another SM103 machine (152 SMs) the heuristic happens to land on a faster kernel (~3.1 µs), so the cost of this bug is machine-dependent and easy to miss.

Fix: allocate packed row-major outputs explicitly. Packed outputs are strictly better for every downstream consumer of these tensors.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py
```

Adds `test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_outputs_are_packed`, which feeds column slices of a fused buffer (the real call pattern from `mla.py`) at `num_tokens ∈ {1, 16}` and asserts packed output strides plus numerical correctness. The `num_tokens == 1` case fails before this change (`stride (768, 1) != (192, 1)`) and passes after.

End-to-end A/B on Kimi-K3, TP8, single 8×GPU SM103 node (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, isl 128 / osl 32, torch-profiled serving, identical config exc …[truncated]
